articles.title: European Union Imposes Customs Tariffs on Fast-Fashion Imports
articles.content: Sign up now: Get ST's newsletters delivered to your inbox The fee will apply to each type of item in a package sent directly to consumers from outside the EU, regardless of the parcel’s value. PHOTO: REUTERS Published Nov 01, 2026, 09:57 AM Updated Nov 01, 2026, 09:57 AM Set as preferred source Summarise The EU introduced a €2 handling fee on parcels from outside the bloc to curb the flood of cheap imports, especially from China, before the holiday shopping rush. The fee applies to each item type in a parcel and adds to the €3 duty on small packages. The EU says consumers should not pay extra, but BEUC fears platforms may pass on costs. Officials say nearly six billion small parcels entered the EU in 2025, with 93% from China. The fee is permanent, while the €3 duty lasts until July 1, 2028. AI generated BRUSSELS – The European Union slapped a €2 (S$2.90) handling fee on packages from outside the 27-nation bloc on Nov 1 in a bid to curb the influx from China. The new levy – coming just weeks before the Black Friday, Cyber Monday, and Christmas season shopping rushes – will be on top of the EU’s three-euro fee on small parcels. The fee will apply to each type of item in a package sent directly to consumers from outside the EU, regardless of the parcel’s value. For example, if there are 10 T-shirts in a package, the handling fee will be €2. But if a package contains two hats and 10 T-shirts, the fee will be €4. The handling fee comes on top of the €3 duty imposed in July on small packages worth less than €150. European consumers are not expected to pay the handling fee, insists the EU, but online retailers and sellers can add a €2 charge before a sale. The European Consumer Organisation (BEUC) said it was “concerned that some platforms may try to pass these new costs onto consumers at the final stages of the purchase”. It added: “That would be illegal under EU law, which requires the full price to be shown upfront.” Nearly six billion small packages entered the EU in 2025, according to official data. Some 93% of the cheap packages that arrived in Europe came from China, usually via popular Asian platforms such as AliExpress and Temu. Brussels says this is putting increasing strain on customs authorities, thereby raising their costs too. The handling fee will compensate their efforts. Since the EU imposed the €3 duty on small parcels in July, imports have fallen by around 64% – although officials warn it is too early to draw firm conclusions. Europe has also expressed concern about “unsafe” non-EU products such as toys that violate the bloc’s rules arriving via Chinese e-commerce platforms. “For years customs have been asked to take on illegal imports with limited resources while small parcels have multiplied out of control,” BEUC’s Agustin Reyna said. The €2 handling fee is a permanent levy but the €3 duty on low-value packages is a temporary measure in place until July 1, 2028. From that date onwards, standard, product-specific customs tariffs will apply. The EU will have to assess the handling fee’s amount every two years to ensure it remains proportional to the cost of customs operations in the bloc. articles.title: Crypto PACs Deploy Two Hundred Million to Capture Midterm Races
articles.content: LivestreamMenuCryptocurrency groups make up the largest cohort of single-issue super PACs in U.S. history, injecting millions of dollars into the 2026 midterm elections, according to Public Citizen.The digital asset industry is hoping to sway races across the country two years after spending about $250 million to elect pro-crypto candidates in 2024.A top priority for the industry is getting a comprehensive market structure bill for digital assets across the finish line after the Clarity Act stalled in the Senate. In this article The largest group of single-issue super PACs in United States history is pouring millions of dollars into congressional races across the country. Cryptocurrency groups outpaced online betting and data center development groups in federal corporate political spending this election cycle, according to Public Citizen. Crypto-tied organizations have contributed more than $200 million in this election cycle. The industry is hoping to repeat the success of 2024, when super PACs spent $250 million to elect pro-crypto lawmakers and reshape Congress. Crypto juggernaut Fairshake and its affiliated super PACs are throwing their support behind 33 House candidates — 19 Republicans and 14 Democrats — seen as key supporters of the industry's priorities. The network is prioritizing six House incumbents by injecting a baseline of $1 million into their campaigns. Republicans Bryan Steil of Wisconsin, who chairs a digital assets subcommittee in the lower chamber, as well as French Hill of Arkansas and Bill Huizenga of Michigan, who serve as the chair and vice chair of the House Financial Services Committee, respectively. Democratic lawmakers receiving at least $1 million from Fairshake include Reps. Janelle Bynum of Oregon; Derek Tran of California; and Steven Horsford of Nevada. Fairshake's spending spree has been supercharged by digital asset-focused companies, like cryptocurrency exchange Coinbase Global. Coinbase established itself as one of the largest corporate political donors in modern history in the 2024 election cycle, contributing $79 million to federal races, according to OpenSecrets. That included a $1 million dollar personal contribution from CEO Brian Armstrong to Fairshake in 2023. Coinbase donated $25 million to Fairshake's midterm efforts in 2025, according to the super PAC. "The ultimate goal is to make sure that we bring our 20th century financial system into the 21st century," Ryan VanGrack, vice chairman at Coinbase, told CNBC. "In an era where affordability is top of mind for American voters, it's important that we find a way that we can move money more cheaply, that we can invest more easily, and that we can transact more quickly, and fundamentally that is not something that Democrats or Republicans should oppose," he said. The industry faced pushback in the current Congress as it urged lawmakers to pass landmark crypto legislation. In September, the Clarity Act, a bipartisan set of market structure rules for digital assets, stalled in the Senate after Democrats argued it didn't do enough to prevent top government officials from profiting off crypto ventures. The stalemate over ethics comes as Americans grow increasingly gloomy toward government corruption. A Gallup poll released in September found a record 89% of U.S. adults say government corruption is widespread. Changing voter priorities also present a headwind for crypto's legislative efforts. The latest CNBC All-America Economic Survey this month found only 20% of respondents rate the economy as excellent or good, down from 27% in July. "Overwhelmingly, the issue right now is the affordability crisis," said Rep. Steven Horsford (D-Nev.), one of the three Democratic candidates Fairshake is giving more than $1 million. Horsford, who introduced bipartisan legislation in May to modernize federal tax laws for digital assets, said crypto is still on the minds of some voters, alongside economic uncertainty. "It definitely comes up in town halls and community meetings, in forums that I have, especially with small businesses who are looking to use digital assets and bitcoin," said Horsford. "They're being asked more and more by their consumers whether or not they take those those payments for services and goods." November's elections will test crypto's continued influence on Washington. The crypto industry is laser-focused on the Ohio Senate race between Democratic nominee, and former Senator, Sherrod Brown, a longtime crypto critic, and Republican Jon Husted, who is pro-crypto and currently holds the seat. Fairshake spent about $40 million to unseat Brown in 2024, when the then-Senate Banking Committee chairman had promoted tougher crypto regulation and stalled a House-passed market-structure bill. The super PAC this cycle told CNBC it has already spent $55 million to oppose Brown. A Marist poll conducted Oct. 15-18 showed Brown holding a four-point edge over Husted among likely voters statewide, within the margin of error of 4.5%. "A lot of these races are going to be extremely tight," said Mason Lynaugh, executive director of the advocacy group Stand With Crypto, launched by Coinbase in 2023. This election cycle, Stand With Crypto has endorsed a total of 45 candidates, 42 in the House of Representatives and three in the Senate. Lynaugh told CNBC one of the reasons the group endorses candidates is because of their legislative record. "We want to show that when we execute our program and we turn out those thousands or tens of thousands of Stand With Crypto advocates in these districts we are credibly ensuring that they get what they deserve for supporting crypto from the community that supports them," he added. Digital assets and infrastructure company Ripple spent a total of $63.65 million in federal contributions last election, according to OpenSecrets, and the company is spending millions again now. Ripple donated $25 million in 2025, according to Fairshake. Asked if the crypto industry got a good return on its investment, Stu Alderoty, Ripple's chief legal officer, told CNBC, "I think compared to where the industry was two years ago to where the industry is today, yes, I would say that that is a very good return." Alderoty pointed to the GENIUS Act, which established the first federal framework for dollar-pegged stablecoins. President Trump signed the bill into law in July 2025, the first-ever standalone crypto legislation in the United States. Alderoty noted that the industry has gotten clearer rules from both the Securities and Exchange Commission and the Commodity Futures and Trading Commission. He also pointed to advancements for the industry from the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency, noting that Ripple received final OCC approval this week to charter Ripple National Trust Bank, a federally supervised national trust bank. But the latest guidelines from these agencies aren't meant to replace legislation from Congress, and the window to pass new laws for crypto may be closing. Former New York governor Andrew Cuomo, now a board member of the crypto exchange OKX, told CNBC that lawmaking is unlikely if Congress changes hands in January. "You're going to have a Democratic Congress overseeing an administration, the Trump administration, where the regulators are making decisions under the scrutiny of a hostile Congress, and that is not a good place to be because the Congress will be at loggerheads with the administration," he said. Horsford, the Nevada congressman, told CNBC that time is of the essence. "Every stakeholder needs to stay at the table and to continue to make the case why legislation is needed," he said. If the Clarity Act doesn't advance before the end of the year, Congress will have to start from scratch on a new market structure bill for digital assets. And crypto super PACs are hoping their spending still has the influence to shape which lawmakers work on the next round of legislation. "Regardless of who is elected in Congress, we're going to continue to see more regulatory clarity in this space," Coinbase's VanGrack, a former SEC senior advisor, told CNBC. "It may be an open question whether we get all the way across the goal line, but it's not an open question about whether we're going to have progress and continue to see progress in terms of regulatory clarity in crypto," VanGrack added. — CNBC's Luke Fountain contributed to this report.

articles.title: Trillion Dollar Selloff Punishes Big Tech Hardware Capital Expenditures
articles.content: Markets are ushering in a particularly gothic Halloween as the AI trade exposes a crumbling aristocratic pile of early 21st century capitalism. Wall Street has been describing itself in castle-adjacent terms for years. Recommended Video Jamie Dimon has long talked to JPMorgan shareholders about the bank’s “fortress balance sheet.” His 2015 letter set aside a section to answer the question of what the phrase even meant. By 2021, he’d added a second castle word, warning that “the moats that protect this company are not particularly deep.” The moat came from Warren Buffett. In a 1999 Fortune article with Carol Loomis, he argued that the key to investing is a company’s competitive advantage and how durable it is, and that the businesses worth owning have wide moats around them. The gothic novel’s favorite picture of danger is a castle falling apart, and for about 250 years the two have traded images: the castle and the moat, the vampire, the creature built in a lab. This Halloween season has them rushing to the front of the conversation, with a two-day rout in tech stocks on Thursday and Friday turning on whether the AI giants’ moats will hold, as gothic horror booms on bookshelves and movie screens. Horror took 15.5% of the domestic box office in 2025, according to The Numbers , and U.S. horror book sales rose 7% through the first nine months of 2025, per Circana BookScan , while adult fiction overall grew just 1% . The New York Times asked Friday why every book is gothic now , with publishers putting the label on everything from family sagas to space operas, and several film critics commenting that Nathan Fielder’s smash-hit business-scandal documentary You Can See Everything is a twisted , even gothic romance in the tradition of Alfred Hitchcock. The selling started with Alphabet . The stock fell 12.6% Thursday , wiping out roughly half a trillion dollars in market value, after the Google parent’s quarterly report. Revenue from the core search unit fell short, partly because of the popularity of less-profitable “AI mode” searches and the company burning cash faster than expected. Its free cash flow came in at negative $9.1 billion, against the negative $2.23 billion analysts expected, per FactSet . The S&P 500’s worst performer was software giant ServiceNow , which dropped 27% the same day on slowing revenue growth and disappointing guidance. By Friday morning, it was Amazon’s and Intel’s turn, with Intel down roughly 25% before the opening bell. Big Tech lost nearly $900 billion in market value after another sharp rise in AI spending in the third quarter, the Financial Times calculated. Nasdaq 100 companies lost more than $1 trillion in market value Friday alone. Reddit, whose shares fell more than 22% premarket Friday, is pulling up the drawbridge: it’s moving to a logged-in experience as AI eats search. The irony is spooking investors. AI is eating into the businesses that throw off the cash, and the cash is going into AI anyway. The hyperscalers have raised $326 billion in stock and bonds this year to pay for the build-out, more than triple 2025, according to S&P Global Market Intelligence data. The question underneath it is the one Apollo chief economist Torsten Slok put to clients the morning Alphabet fell. “With AI disruption potentially around the corner, there is a lot of discussion about moats at the moment,” he wrote in his Daily Spark note Thursday. He built on finance professor Aswath Damodaran, the “dean of valuation,” who compiled a list of sources of competitive advantage, including brand strength, switching costs, network effects, cost advantages and legal protection. Then he boiled it down to an AI moat checklist of three questions: does the company own data its rivals can’t get, is its product part of how customers do their jobs every day, and can it charge more without customers walking away? Judging by that third test, the companies selling AI don’t seem to measure up. OpenAI’s new GPT-6.1 Terra model costs up to half as much per token as the version before it. An index from expense-management firm Ramp, which looked at what companies actually pay Anthropic and OpenAI, shows token prices down roughly 35% since the end of June, in what Axios called a price war. The companies paying for AI aren’t getting much back yet, either. In an Oct. 24 note, Slok sent a tremor through Wall Street terminals with an argument that AI “has delivered zero financial payoff to corporate America outside of tech.” Revenue per worker and profit margins are rising for the Magnificent Seven and flat for the rest of the S&P 500, he noted, and mainstream companies are starting to treat token spending as a cost center that weighs on margins rather than a source of growth. Xavier Aldana Reyes, a researcher at the Manchester Centre for Gothic Studies, told the Times that interest in the gothic tends to surge during periods of social anxiety and political turmoil. Literary agent Mary C. Moore put the genre’s subject more bluntly, telling the paper that “Gothics are all about exposing what is rotten at the core of something shiny/wealthy.” The genre was invented by a scion of wealth who knew the old order from inside and drew a salary without working at all. Horace Walpole was the son of UK Prime Minister Robert Walpole, and his The Castle of Otranto , published in 1764, is generally regarded as the first gothic novel. He passed it off as a translation of an obscure Italian work, found in the library of an old Catholic family in northern England and printed at Naples in 1529. But it was really his dramatization of the aristocratic system being usurped by the “greedy” new bourgeoisie, per a 2014 paper by Çankaya University’s Ertuğrul Koç and Neslihan Atcan Altan. The literary historian Robert Miles has written that the modern novel itself was understood to have been revolutionized by print technology, which made the circulating library possible, and explains Walpole’s pre-modern faux origin story. We all know which gothic tales came next. In her 1831 introduction to Frankenstein , Mary Shelley said the idea came to her in June 1816 after she overheard Lord Byron and Percy Shelley discussing galvanic experiments. A 2018 piece republished by Live Science made the comparison directly: electrical life stirred up the same range of arguments then that AI does now. Karl Marx made the trade official. In Capital , in 1867, he wrote that capital is “dead labour, that, vampire-like, only lives by sucking living labour,” an image that turns up across 30 years of his writing. Bram Stoker’s Dracula created the great modern vampire myth in 1897, landing as a depression in agriculture threatened the fortunes and estates of Britain’s noblemen, even as a cheap agricultural products flooded in from booming American farms. The literary critic Franco Moretti read the count as a businessman. In a 1982 essay in New Left Review , he described Stoker’s Dracula as a rational entrepreneur who invests his gold to expand his dominion and conquer the City of London. In more recent times, Matt Taibbi’s 2009 Rolling Stone story “The Great American Bubble Machine” called Goldman Sachs “a great vampire squid wrapped around the face of humanity.” The line stuck well enough that then-Goldman CEO Lloyd Blankfein conceded in August of that year that the article had “tapped into something.” Economists got their own monster: zombie firms. Bank for International Settlements researchers Ryan Banerjee and Boris Hofmann define them as companies at least 10 years old whose earnings haven’t covered their interest payments for three straight years. Across 14 advanced economies, the zombie share of listed non-financial companies rose from 4% in the late 1980s to 15% in 2017 . The researchers found that weak banks that roll over loans instead of writing them off keep zombie companies on life support, and that lower interest rates tend to push the zombie share up. The newest candidates are in software. PitchBook counted $131 billion of leveraged loans priced below 80 cents on the dollar, a common threshold for distress and the most since May 2020. Software companies account for 32% of those distressed loans while making up just 12% of the index, and 84% of stressed software companies are backed by private equity. These are castles that can’t pay their own upkeep, kept standing by somebody else’s money, the dollar-princess arrangement with a credit line instead of a dowry. The anxiety is big business for the haunted boom of 2026. Book publisher Zando launched a horror imprint , Evil Twin, planning six to eight titles a year. In Hollywood, Warner Bros.’ R-rated body-horror film Clayface opened No. 1 the weekend of Oct. 23 with about $24 million, according to The Numbers . The machines are writing the stuff now, too. Inkfluence AI, a fiction-writing platform, says 3,929 horror books were started on it in the 180 days to Sept. 12, with haunted-house and ghost premises leading at about a third. articles.title: Quad Ministers Mobilize Critical Supply Chains to Counter Chinese Controls
articles.content: By Andrea Shalal Oct 31, 2026 Add AL-MONITOR on Google G20 foreign ministers' meeting in Atlanta, Georgia — Erik S. Lesser By Andrea Shalal ATLANTA, Oct 31 (Reuters) - Foreign ministers from the US, Australia, India and Japan on Saturday pledged to work on building reliable global supply chains and expressed grave concerns about what they called "economic coercion" through export restrictions and non-market practices, but stopped short of calling out China. The joint statement by the foreign ministers of the Indo-Pacific "Quad" came at a time when Japan has been extremely critical of Beijing over its restrictions on critical mineral exports, and the US has been assembling a coalition aimed at uniting G20 countries concerned about China's dominance in rare earths and other critical minerals. The meeting was held shortly before US Secretary of State Marco Rubio hosted the final session of a meeting in Atlanta of foreign ministers from the broader Group of 20 major economies, which includes China. The Quad ministers reiterated their support for a free and open Indo-Pacific, underscoring the importance of economic security in maintaining global stability and prosperity, including through reliable and open global supply chains. "They expressed grave concerns regarding economic coercion, including through arbitrary export restrictions, as well as non-market policies and practices that result in overcapacity to disrupt global supply chains in critical industries," the joint statement said. The ministers also emphasized the "absolute necessity to protect and preserve navigational rights and freedoms in the Strait of Hormuz, the Red Sea, and the Bab el-Mandeb Strait," the statement said. The group pledged more than $85 million in assistance to support trusted artificial intelligence technologies across the Indo-Pacific region and said it would launch a new effort to identify vulnerabilities in semiconductor and related supply chains before they cause disruptions. It was the third meeting of the Quad foreign ministers this year, with plans taking shape for US President Donald Trump to attend his first formal meeting of the leaders of the four countries next month in Manila during a conference of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations. Rubio told reporters that a Quad leaders meeting in Manila would "hopefully" be announced very soon, but gave no further details. He said the Quad was not "an anti-China or anti-anybody coalition," adding that the joint statement was raising concerns about behaviors and activities that he said were "coming repetitively from one country." He said the US had invested a lot of time in the Quad group and wanted to continue to build on its work on specific projects and initiatives, including a $20 million project in Palau aimed at improving its digital infrastructure. Rubio said the four countries had already made substantial progress in ensuring they could pool resources in the event of a humanitarian crisis or national disaster, and also planned to set up a business forum so that businesses in all four nations could find new opportunities to work together. articles.title: Taiwan Raids Military Drone Contractor Over Chinese Chips
articles.content: Add TT as Preferred Source Three government agencies had purchased a total of 32 drones made by or linked to Align Corp (亞拓科技), the Ministry of the Interior said yesterday, after the company’s director was detained for allegedly using Chinese-made chips in military drones. The ministry said it would act in accordance with the Government Procurement Act (政府採購法) and contractual provisions, adding that it would not rule out seeking compensation if any contraventions were found. A preliminary review found that the National Park Service and Central Police University each purchased one drone manufactured by the company last year, the ministry said, adding that it would verify the details and handle the matter in accordance with procurement regulations. Separately, the National Immigration Agency (NIA) this year completed a public tender under the Government Procurement Act to purchase 30 drones from Suyuan Technology Co (速源科技) at a total cost of NT$2.75 million (US$84,673), the ministry said. While Suyuan Technology had planned to supply the drones manufactured by Align, delivery has not yet taken place, it said. The NIA would strictly enforce contractual requirements prohibiting the delivery of drones containing Chinese-made components, it said. As government procurement standards mandate compliance with “non-red supply chain” requirements, the ministry would continue to strictly require government agencies and suppliers to follow the regulations in procurement processes, it said. Compensation would be sought in accordance with contractual terms if contraventions were found, it added. The ministry’s review came as the Taichung Prosecutors’ Office on Friday said that it raided Align Corp and the company’s director Tu Ta-sen (杜大森) was ordered detained and held incommunicado. The company’s drones were purchased by the army for educational and training purposes, it said To ensure the equipment met procurement specifications, the military conducted inspections that included dismantling the drones and discovered that chips inside the aircraft bore the letters “CN,” it said. The procurement contracts explicitly prohibit the use of products from China, Hong Kong and Macau, it said. The case was reported to prosecutors who found the same issue in another batch of drones purchased by the army. Prosecutors searched locations connected to the company and summoned six people for questioning, including Tu and his wife, they said. Investigators found that Tu allegedly used chips manufactured by Chinese companies in at least two batches of military drone procurement contracts and directed Align Corp to assemble the drones before delivering them to the military, they said. The contracts were worth more than NT$8 million in total, they added. Tu and others were suspected of misrepresenting the country of origin of products supplied under the contracts, they said. They were suspected of contravening the National Security Act (國家安全法), which prohibits the delivery of products for military procurement when the supplier knows they originate in China, and also face fraud charges under the Criminal Code, they said. Align Corp, founded in 1984, is headquartered in Taichung’s Fengyuan District (豐原), the company’s Web site showed. The terms of the agreement are confidential, but sources close to Meta told AFP the company decided to settle for business reasons. “Trials, dismissals and settlements are all common in the bellwether process, and this litigation is no exception,” a Meta spokesperson said, referring to the series of test cases against the company being tried in Los Angeles. If Snap does not settle, the trial will go ahead next week. Snap did not immediately respond to a request for comment. TikTok and YouTube were also named as defendants in the case, but both had already reached settlements with the plaintiffs, known by their initials SJ and KDB, their lawyers said. Meta had also previously settled with SJ. A California state judge consolidated the two cases into a single trial. Snap, which makes Snapchat, will defend itself against the claims of both SJ and KDB. Lawyers for SJ and KDB will argue that their clients were exposed to “addictive and problematic” social media apps when they started using them at ages 13 and 15, respectively, according to court documents. “We believe the evidence will support that we have put our community first, and that these allegations fundamentally misrepresent the plaintiffs’ experiences on Snapchat and how our platform was designed,” a Snap spokesperson said in a statement earlier this week. Thousands of lawsuits have been filed in recent years in local, state and federal courtrooms across the country with various claims about alleged harms to children and teenagers caused by social media companies. The cases – the first of which went to trial earlier in 2026 in Los Angeles – have taken twists and turns. Meta and YouTube lost the first so-called bellwether case earlier in 2026, when a jury found them collectively liable for harming a young user known by the initials KGM, and ordered the tech companies to pay a combined US$6 million (S$7.67 million) penalty . Snap and TikTok settled with KGM ahead of that trial. Months later, Snap, TikTok and YouTube settled another case that was set to go to trial in August; that plaintiff, known as RKC, then withdrew their remaining claims against Meta , allowing the Instagram and Facebook maker to avoid trial without a settlement. By settling before a trial kicks off, the social media companies contain costs from lawyer fees and potential penalties; another benefit is that it shields their executives from testifying in court. Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg and Instagram chief Adam Mosseri were expected to be called as key witnesses in the upcoming Los Angeles trial. Snap CEO Evan Spiegel is expected to testify if the trial proceeds without another settlement. In August, Meta agreed to pay more than US$18 billion in penalties, in addition to making changes to Instagram and Facebook for teens , when it settled with 52 attorneys general several days into a trial held in California. That settlement came just a day after Mosseri testified, and before Zuckerberg had been called to the stand. Meta has faced other trials, though. Earlier in October, a New Mexico judge ordered Meta to pay $25 billion in a case where the company was found liable for deceiving users in the state about how their data was used in a case related to the Cambridge Analytica scandal. A New Mexico jury also found the social media giant liable for harms to children, leading to a combined penalty of US$942 million earlier in 2026. AFP Meta Social media United States

articles.title: China Positions Digital Yuan as Secondary Global Trade Alternative
articles.content: Heavy is the head that wears the crown, and contrary to popular belief, Beijing doesn’t want the yuan to dethrone the dollar as the world’s dominant currency, according to a top China scholar. Recommended Video While China has been trying to internationalize the yuan, also known as the renminbi, it doesn’t want the obligations that come with being the global reserve currency, Zongyuan Zoe Liu, senior fellow for China studies at the Council on Foreign Relation, wrote in Foreign Affairs this month. To truly take the dollar’s place would require open capital markets, which would threaten the Communist Party’s control over who gets capital and how, she explained. That’s as many elites rely on offshore dollar holdings as a type of insurance against domestic political persecution. Since China actually prefers to keep the dollar on top, the real reason for promoting the yuan abroad is to prevent the U.S. from weaponizing the financial system against it, Liu added, similar to how Russia was shut out after it invaded Ukraine in 2022. A yuan network that’s international enough, even without being dominant, could bypass any dollar-based sanctions the U.S. might impose in the future. “Placing a respectable second, or even a consequential third, would suffice to break the dollar’s effective monopoly and constrain the United States’ ability to impose financial sanctions unilaterally, while saving China the effort and cost of sustaining currency supremacy,” she said. “From Beijing’s perspective, the mission is to establish the renminbi as the Pepsi to the dollar’s Coca-Cola: never the market leader, but serviceable in a pinch and more than capable of keeping the dominant incumbent honest.” (For what it’s worth, Pepsi has actually fallen further behind Coke in the cola wars and was dealt a major symbolic defeat recently when KFC said it would replace PepsiCo soft drinks with Coca-Cola’s products at its 3,700 U.S. restaurants.) So far, China facilitates renminbi use among firms in more than a hundred countries and across a growing array of commodity markets. As of June, its Cross-Border Interbank Payment System had 1,829 participants who could send payments to more than 5,200 banks in 191 countries. But that’s just a small fraction of what the U.S.-dominated system processes, Liu said, adding that a global currency also entails pricing, financing, risk transfer, and reinvestment. Chinese exporters still invoice in dollars and convert them to yuan just before brining them into China. But Beijing is promoting “China prices,” or yuan benchmarks on domestic commodity exchanges and has succeeded with lithium, she noted. The financing stage is gaining momentum too as Chinese banks have more than doubled their yuan lending to overseas borrowers between 2023 and mid-2026. The People’s Bank of China has also reached currency swap agreements with 32 foreign central banks and monetary authorities. More modest steps have increased the yuan’s presence in risk transfer markets as state firms have begun settling cargo insurance in yuan. But reinvestment is perhaps the weakest link in the chain. A strong yuan ecosystem requires recipients to hold and reinvest their balances rather than convert them, Liu argued. China has expanded overseas access to domestic stocks and bonds, but Beijing’s unpredictable capital controls remain a worry. In March, foreign investors held just 1.6% of the Chinese bond market versus 27% in the U.S. bond market. “Without a far larger pool of renminbi assets that foreigners can freely buy and sell, the renminbi cannot come close to replacing the dollar,” she said. But similar to how the “petrodollar” anchors the greenback’s role in global trade, the yuan can dominate trade in an essential good that China controls. That could take the form of critical minerals, clean energy equipment, and electrical infrastructure used in green energy technology, Liu posited. China has already established supremacy across much of the green supply chain and is promoting standards built around technologies Chinese-owned firms. “If China consolidates its dominance over that industrial ecosystem, using its scale and cost advantages to prevent competitors from catching up, it could gain enough leverage to price those essential, hard-to-substitute exports in renminbi, creating the foundation for a ‘green yuan’ that might eventually replace the petrodollar,” she predicted. Meanwhile, the Iran war has raised doubts about the petrodollar , which goes back to a deal struck in 1974 when Saudi Arabia agreed to price its oil in dollars and invest surpluses in U.S. assets. In exchange for Saudi Arabia recycling its dollars back into the U.S., Washington guaranteed the kingdom’s security, which also involved stationing troops in the region, providing advanced weapons, and ensuring free navigation in the Strait of Hormuz. But America’s role in the Mideast looks vastly different today. Despite 40 days of punishing bombardment of Iran and round-the-clock protection of commercial ships, the U.S. still hasn’t fully restored traffic in the strait. At the same time, Iran’s swarms of missiles and drones have inflicted significant damage on U.S. aircraft, radars and bases, while American air-defense systems have failed to completely protect Gulf allies’ critical energy infrastructure. “Damage to Gulf economies could encourage an unwind in their foreign asset savings,” Deutsche Bank warned in March. “In this context, reports that the passage for ships through the Strait of Hormuz may be granted in exchange for oil payments in yuan should be closely followed. The conflict could be remembered as a key catalyst for erosion in petrodollar dominance, and the beginnings of the petroyuan.” Fortune Daily breaks the traditional barrier between audience and newsroom. The show transforms Fortune ’s trusted reporting into actionable, conversational, and entertaining insights for an emerging class of business leaders. Watch here.

articles.title: Silicon Valley Startups Conceal Human Labor Behind Autonomous Agents
articles.content: LivestreamMenuThe next time someone's supercharged AI agent attempts to make a phone call to negotiate a cable bill, it could be an actual human who haggles with customer service.Foundation models developed by companies like Meta and OpenAI still can't reliably take actions across the web, particularly those involving phone calls. Marissa Mayer's Dazzle AI and other personal AI agent startups like Duckbill and Wajo AI are all emphasizing the role human workers play in accomplishing tasks when software fails.Various examples of avatars for Muse, Meta's AI Agent, during the Meta Connect event in Menlo Park, California, US, on Wednesday, Sept. 23, 2026. Minh Connors | Bloomberg | Getty ImagesThe next time someone's supercharged AI agent attempts to make a phone call to negotiate a cable bill, it could be an actual human who haggles with customer service rather than the software. That's because AI agents, powered by the bleeding-edge foundation models developed by companies like Meta and OpenAI, still can't reliably take actions across the web, particularly those involving phone calls. Former Yahoo CEO Marissa Mayer, who now helms agent startup Dazzle AI, says current top-tier AI models excel at surfacing online home renovation services for consumers, but might blow it when they need to book and schedule a rooftop upgrade. "We're relying on the frontier models to give us good suggestions and a good candidate list, but we're checking that over to make sure that we're really delivering the type of service that we can stand behind," Mayer said, referring to how Dazzle funnels certain tasks to human contractors. Digital assistants driven by artificial intelligence are currently gaining renewed interest thanks to Meta, OpenAI and others that are pitching the technology as capable of tasks like scouting the internet for shoes. Meta's Muse, OpenAI's Dots and a host of other agents can accomplish a multitude of web-browsing feats, but it's still early days for the technology, and it often hits digital roadblocks. Those barriers typically involve tasks that would have an AI agent make a phone call, schedule a doctor's appointment on someone's behalf, or reserve a couch scrubbing from a local cleaning service, said Meghan Joyce, CEO of digital agent startup Duckbill. For tasks that require real-world judgment, Joyce said humans still trump AI, and companies building consumer-grade digital assistants will need to patch in real people to take over. That's why Duckbill recently debuted an application programming interface, or API, intended for companies building personal agents to connect with human contract workers. "We work on a model that is not dissimilar from Uber, where we boil tasks down into atomic bite-sized pieces," Joyce said, referencing the ride-hailing company where she previously worked. Companies making agents can use Duckbill's API to delegate the tasks that the agent is likely to fumble. Duckbill translates those tasks into bite-sized pieces that the average adult can do consistently and reliably. "And then we track what happens," Joyce said. Mayer said that AI models can still lack common sense. She said a Dazzle AI super user attempted to have the technology simultaneously handle a series of home renovation projects involving a roof replacement, a broken window and the purchase of a glass tabletop. But the AI agent, Mayer said, confused window glass with tabletop glass, resulting in the digital assistant "trying to figure out if he could make the tabletop fit in the window." The mishap didn't last long, Mayer said, because Dazzle's technology flagged the task and outsourced it to a person to complete. "Within a few seconds, the human had things sorted out. Whereas an agent would have burned a ridiculous number of tokens," Mayer said. "Or they may never have gotten to a good solution." Shivani Poddar, CEO of personal AI agent startup Wajo AI, is also incorporating human workers to handle phone calls and even CAPTCHA tests intended to fend off bots from sites. "I think AI plus humans, collaborative AI, is what you need to actually get the job done," Poddar said, emphasizing that people will stop using the technology if agents can't complete tasks. Chatbot and agent interactions can be ultra personal and users have good reason to be concerned about the humans stepping in, particularly if the company didn't tell them how it works. Meta employees previously raised privacy concerns about the company's internal test using human contractors to handle phone calls on behalf of its Muse AI agent. A Meta spokesperson said in a statement at the time that this kind of testing is "core to the product development process." Meta currently doesn't use humans to complete users' Muse requests. Duckbill's Joyce said her startup does "full background checking" into the 1099 contractors it uses, comparing them to drivers for Uber and DoorDash, "people who live here in the United States and want a source of additional income." Duckbill also uses contract workers from businesses that typically offer contact center labor to companies. Mayer said Dazzle conducts background checks and looks for contractors with the same qualities someone might look for in a human personal assistant. "We generally are screening for people who we think are extremely discreet and have good taste and good judgment, both in terms of how they interact with our users, but just the ability to kind of forget and compartmentalize that information afterwards," Mayer said. "I understand it's a point of privilege, but I've had personal assistants for some time, and I know how I want them, and I know how I guide them." Mayer said that while foundation models are still improving, the market is in a "transitionary period" until the technology can perform more involved web tasks and phone calls as efficiently as people. "We're not even trying to hide it, we think the human in the loop is a benefit," Mayer said. WATCH: Who's liable when AI agents break the rules?

While single-family property owners charge overnight using discounted residential electricity, 44 million multi-family households remain stranded without reliable charging access. According to multiple user claims, Anthropic's Claude Code and/or Opus 5.5 model are blocking attempts at innocuous reverse-engineering, including but not limited to those using the popular Reverse Engineer Anything (REA) tool. That issue may be linked to a text rule that's now in force, which allegedly instructs the model to avoid "[recreating] a specific existing game." The updated rule appears to be a move to limit a flood of AI-cracked and cloned titles, with some game devs even recently being hit by extortion scams that threaten to clone their game demos into complete games before they have a chance to finish and release the original. According to Twitter user Chasm, the game-related textual rule is "Do build original games, games in a genre, and games from the user’s own designs and assets. Don’t build a recreation of a specific existing game, even if it is renamed or called original." There is no official or additional confirmation if this is the actual rule text, but it's plausible enough given the very clear refusals that devs have been encountering over the past week. This situation is tricky to analyze due to the varying types of reports. First, the existence of a game-related rule is real, as Claude Code's GitHub is seeing an influx of issues complaining about refusals to do standard game work halfway through development , when replicating a game mechanic , and patching a tabletop-like game . It's possible that some of those reports have been made by users with nefarious purposes, but at least one is a bona fide developer with a real track record . As for reverse engineering, there had already been a smattering of user reports across Reddit and other platforms, wherein Claude refused to perform tasks like (allegedly) analyzing a simple Windows crash dump, clearing up junkware on a Samsung TV, or just using REA altogether. Latest Videos From Tom's Hardware The simultaneous timing of both game- and cyber- security restrictions may be a coincidence, and yet there are complaints from purported game developers saying that Claude blocked their own games' anti-cheat development and security reviews , under the justification that its safeguards were triggered. Anthropic introduced its Cyber Verification Program on October 6, essentially saying that access to its frontier models' advanced cybersecurity capabilities would be limited to entities covered by Project Glasswing , taking effect immediately. It's possible that whichever ruleset was applied is the same one that's causing the cybersecurity-related refusals. Still, it's odd to see that 24 days have passed since then, and yet reports of bot refusal are only coming in since the last week or so. As for possible motivations behind these restrictions, they are twofold. The first and most obvious one is that Anthropic — and, by extension, other AI players — are preemptively protecting themselves from potential lawsuits from software companies, including game studios, for offering the means to reverse-engineer their software. The recent rash of AI-powered clones of application suites like Adobe's suite and Microsoft Office 365 , as well as the countless recomps and decomps of console games, likely has most every software company on earth rethinking their life choices. And probably also in frequent contact with their legal teams. The online reaction was swift, suggesting that users looking to perform reverse-engineering work simply use Chinese, open-weight, or local LLMs instead of Claude or GPT. This, at the same time, highlights the irony of frontier AI companies that copied the world's information and art for their training sets and are now concerned with copyright infringement. And yet there are situations that merit some discussion, like the recent controversy about the Steam Next Fest being chock-full of AI slop copied from existing titles. That particular situation is getting particularly nasty, as game developers are reportedly being extorted under threat that their game demos will be cloned into complete games before they have a chance to finish and release the original. Adding insult to injury, this is seemingly being done to small studios whose main priority is usually "having food," rather than big publishers looking to microtransaction everything into a new yacht for shareholders. articles.title: Anthropic Disclaims Enterprise Liability Over Poisoned Claude Code Extension Packages
articles.content: Claudeshop fingers 'malicious actor' in targeted supply-chain attack on Cursor Connor Jones Connor Jones Cybersecurity reporter Published fri 30 Oct 2026 // 16:27 UTC Make us preferred on Google Crim spent $7K+ on AI services in extortion attacks, then left evidence for all to see 1 day ago GM cracks the petty cash box for multistate driver tracking settlement 1 day ago British intelligence agency misplaced 'thousands' of storage devices, years later still can't say how many 1 day ago In the year AI re-wrote the infosec rulebook, it’s comforting to know crypto exchanges still have bad security 1 day ago Researchers find bugs in 5 AI developer tools, with OpenAI and Microsoft flaws still unpatched 1 day ago Anthropic has denied allegations that a malicious version of the official Claude Code extension published to Cursor’s marketplace was linked to any kind of compromise of its own systems. The company was forced to issue a statement after prominent figures in the cybersecurity industry alleged that the extension, which infected up to 5,000 developers, was uploaded to Cursor’s marketplace following a breach at Claudemaker Towers. Felix Rieseberg, a member of Anthropic’s technical staff, Xeeted today: "We're working with Cursor on this incident, but it wasn’t a compromise of Anthropic's systems or employee laptops.  "A malicious actor used access to Cursor's marketplace to publish a tampered copy of the Claude Code extension, which we didn't build or publish. The versions on our official channels are not affected, and this only impacts Cursor users." First spotted by EDR vendor Phorion , an unknown party pushed an update to Cursor's official Claude Code extension for Visual Studio Code that contained a persistent SSH backdoor written for Windows, macOS, and Linux. According to Cursor, the extension – version 2.1.313 – was available to download for around 11 hours between 0227 and 1335 PT (0927 and 2035 UTC) on Thursday. The vendors' analyses of the implant revealed that it collected information about the host machine and user, including usernames, configured Git emails, and public IP addresses, as well as attempting to open a reverse SSH tunnel. Crucially, Cursor echoed Phorion's assessment that the package contained a critical flaw.  The script responsible for opening the SSH tunnel required admin rights on macOS and Windows to do so, and in the vast majority of cases it did not have these, resulting in failure. Regardless, the extension still forwards the collected host and user data to the attacker, as well as dropping the attacker's SSH key and installing the persistence mechanism, so developers must go threat hunting in case their instance allows for the SSH tunnel to be created successfully. Simply installing the latest version of the extension is not enough to clear the persistence mechanism, either. The full details of how to remediate the issue, and links to download scripts to wipe the infection, are laid out in Cursor's account of the situation . Aside from Rieseberg's statement today, neither Cursor nor Anthropic have commented on how the malicious package made its way to the official marketplace. Anthropic's position is that a malicious actor uploaded the tampered copy to  Cursor , but the latter has not outlined how it reached the marketpplace. "[We] removed the malicious version from the marketplace immediately upon detection and blocked further distribution," Cursor said in the advisory. "We followed with a full shutdown of the VSCode Marketplace out of an abundance of caution." It also ran checks to confirm no other extensions were compromised in the same way, rotated its own keys before restoring the marketplace, and worked with a cloud hosting provider to block the connection to the attacker's server, it said. ® anthropic cyber-crime security Make us preferred on Google

articles.title: Indian Lender AU Small Finance Bank Probes Dark Web Intrusion
articles.content: AU Small Finance Bank is investigating a potential data leak involving a Salesforce-hosted platform containing vehicle loan customer data, the bank told MediaNama in an email response. The investigation follows a claim by a hacking group on the dark web that it had breached the lender. Cyber threat intelligence account Hackmanac first reported the claim on X. The bank also claims that its own systems are unaffected. Here is the full statement shared with MediaNama: “AU Small Finance Bank is investigating a potential data leak involving a software-as-a-service (SaaS) platform managed and hosted by Salesforce, which holds limited data relating to our vehicle loan customers. We reaffirm that the Bank’s own systems remain unaffected and all banking services are operating normally.” – AU Small Finance Bank  MediaNama reviewed the hacking group’s dark web listing, which claims to include Aadhaar and PAN details, credit reports, signed loan agreements and employee records. The claimed scope is far broader than the “limited data” acknowledged by the bank. However, the group has not publicly released any data samples or the complete datasets. At the time of writing, the listing was marked “negotiation” and displayed a countdown of five days and 17 hours. Redacted screenshots posted by the hackers on the dark web MediaNama could not independently verify that the group holds any original data that belongs to AU Small Finance Bank. We are not naming the group or linking to its website to avoid further exploitation of any data that may have leaked. What the listing describes : The listing categorises the allegedly compromised information as follows, suggesting a broader scope than vehicle loan customer data. We reproduce the description as it appears: “Customer KYC (Core): Per details (name, DOB, PAN, Aadhaar, contact information, family, address, income, education, risk categorq), photos, signatures, CIF/API payloads, field verification notes, and KYC screening records (CKYC. CFR, ICU). Credit and Financial Records: CIBIL reports, FICO scores, address checks, bank statements,_Aadhaar tokens, bureau data, applicant financials, loan applications, approvals, collateral, insurance, disbursements, paqment schedules, and account statements. Signed Loan Documents: e5ign PDFs, loan applications, KFS, sanction letters, MACH mandates, collateral agreements, insurance forms, and supporting ‘documents.” “CRM Person Records: Customer contacts, accounts, addresses, case notes, queries, assignments, work orders, bureau responses, and stored files (ContentVersion).” Staff and Internal Identity: Employee directory, contact details, permissions, group memberships, account teams, roles, login history, IF’ addresses, and audit logs. and much more. ” –  Description of alleged hacked data of AU small finance bank.  The listing also claims employee directories, permissions and audit logs, which the bank has not addressed. The bank’s emphasis on its “own systems” does not answer whether customer data was exposed through a third-party platform.  This development comes at a time when Indian financial institutions are facing multiple cyberattacks. Read more about these cyberattacks here . While reviewing this, MediaNama also found that the same hacker group claims to hold data from Rajasthan Police. The group’s listing describes the allegedly compromised Rajasthan Police data as follows: “witness statements 5,926 Mailboxes 22,686 attachments 68,867 direr-toru records 73,331 identity records 783,435 unique emails 69 verified credentials 21 WPN logins with cleartext. passwords and internal IPs 64 VPN client certificates 13 certificates t.hat. open t.o t.he private key 46 account. ledger entries 6,312 high value t.arget.s 1,1365 tier A senior officer mailboxes” We are not disclosing the website the group says it took the data from. We cannot confirm whether the vulnerabilities it may have exploited have been fixed. We have emailed Rajasthan Police asking for confirmation and a comment. MediaNama will update this report or publish a follow-up article after receiving a response. articles.title: Algorithmic Natural Language Processing Exposes Structural Trauma in Hallucinogen Studies
articles.content: • Scientists Analyzed Thousands of Psychedelic Trips. They Found Something Disturbing · Oct 30, 2026 at 2:00 PM A newly released database of more than 25,000 anonymized calls from the Fireside Project’s Psychedelic Support Line opens a rare window into psychedelic experiences outside of clinical settings. Researchers have amassed a trove of more than 25,000 calls to a support hotline for people during and after psychedelic trips, making it “the largest dataset of psychedelic support interactions ever assembled—exceeding the combined sample sizes of all published psychedelic clinical trials by an order of magnitude,” according to a study published on Friday in Science Advances . Despite the popularity of psychedelics as recreational drugs, and increasing interest in them as medically-prescribed therapeutic treatments, there is very little research about the effects of these substances outside of clinical settings with carefully-selected patients. That, scientists say, is limiting what we can learn about the effects of these drugs, because the vast majority of psychedelics are consumed by all kinds of people in homes, festivals, ceremonial gatherings, or other uncontrolled environments.     The Fireside Project , a nonprofit founded in 2020, has filled this knowledge gap with its Psychedelic Support Line, which connects callers who are on bad trips, or who are seeking more information about psychedelics, with trained volunteers who offer confidential peer support.  🌘 Subscribe to 404 Media to get The Abstract , our newsletter about the most exciting and mind-boggling science news and studies of the week. The team has now published a compendium of 25,419 anonymized interactions with 220 hotline volunteers that took place between April 2021 and February 2026. The database opens an unprecedented window into the experiences of people on psilocybin, ketamine, MDMA, LSD, ayahuasca, and even cannabis, which is not generally considered a psychedelic but can trigger similar effects, such as mild hallucinations.  It’s a “treasure trove,” said Félix Schoeller, a senior research scientist at the Institute for Advanced Consciousness Studies , a California-based nonprofit, who led the study, in a call with 404 Media. “In general, we're really lacking any evidence and data beyond what exists in the underground world, if you will, for psychedelic therapy.”  “There's different types of knowledge,” continued Schoeller, who is CEO of ReWire Neurotechnologies , a startup focused on novel experiential treatments for depression. “Some cultures and communities have been doing that for thousands of years. But there's a question about how to do this in a way that follows the principles of biomedical science.”   The interactions included phone calls and text exchanges with hotline volunteers who provided support by talking through the experience or connecting callers with emergency services in the most urgent cases. About 40.2 percent of callers (10,208 interactions) were actively tripping, while 32.1 percent of callers reached out after they had tripped, a period known as “integration.”   The rest of the calls fell into smaller categories, such as informational inquiries about certain substances, requests to prepare or buy drugs, or calls from “trip-sitters” assisting a person on psychedelics.  Psilocybin was the most commonly reported substance (9,348 callers), followed by LSD (2,247callers), cannabis (2,004 callers), and ketamine (1,194 callers), and MDMA (682 callers), with ayahuasca and other drugs logging much smaller numbers.   Surprisingly, callers who had used cannabis  reported the highest distress rate—47.2 percent had bad experiences with the drug. Though cannabis has a reputation as a low-stakes substance, the study confirms that it can induce real distress in some cases that warrant consideration for harm reduction. The distress rates for the rest of the commonly used psychedelics were only slightly lower than cannabis, ranging between 40 to 42 percent. The study also revealed 43 rare but disturbing instances of “facilitator abuse,” including at remote retreats or ceremonial gatherings involving ayahuasca. In these cases, callers reported abuse from the people providing psychedelics, such as reports they had deliberately been given extra doses without consent.  Those reports “provide the first quantitative documentation of this phenomenon in a community help-seeking sample,” according to the study. “The pattern of these reports—clustering in ceremonial settings involving plant medicines, presenting primarily as trauma-processing calls, and involving callers with elevated rates of prior PTSD diagnoses—suggests that even modest surveillance through existing peer support infrastructure can detect harm occurring in unregulated psychedelic settings.” Some calls also came from people who said they suffered from schizophrenia, or had taken multiple psychedelics, offering a rare glimpse of situations that could not be observed in clinical settings.  “This kind of data can inform us on these topics in the context of legalizing these drugs and making them accessible,” said Schoeller. “I'm glad that there's this data that exists that people can look into to support or contradict the claims that they make as to how these things should be done.”  The study also outlines several limitations, including its sample bias of people who are inclined to call a hotline in the first place—which is not representative of psychedelic consumers at large—as well as self-reported accounts of doses, among other factors that are impossible to verify. Despite the noisiness of the data, however, it contains helpful clues about avenues for future research. In Schoeller’s view, one of the most important revelations was that the success of a call was strongly linked to the perception that the hotline volunteer showed genuine care and empathy toward the caller. Using 2,777 postinteraction satisfaction surveys, the team found that the few negative experiences with the hotline tended to stem from feelings that the volunteer was dismissive, or didn’t seem to care about the caller.  “My takeaway is that the number one thing that predicts whether a support call will not work” is “the volunteer being perceived as genuine,” Schoeller said. “That's something that, in many ways, poses a problem to the biomedical system of centralized hospitals. I'm not trying to be ideological in any way, but when you create a centralized institution where you throw everybody to a single place to get care”  then “clinicians become burned out.” For this reason, Schoeller and his colleagues plan to follow up on the role of perceived care and empathy in treatment, and to emphasize this factor in guidance for community-based peer support for people in crisis due to psychedelics. It also reinforces the value of the Fireside Project’s hotline, which provides a safe and confidential service for people who might be reluctant to contact emergency services because of the criminalization of these substances or fear of incurring medical debt. “For many people, they have experiences with psychedelics, and they may not be required to go to the ER, but they still need someone to help them navigate the difficult experience,” Schoeller concluded. “The hotline can truly be a lifeline for them.”  • •

articles.title: Dutch E-Commerce Champion Bol Fortifies Logistics Against Chinese Algorithmic Retailers
articles.content: Als ceo van de grootste boekenwinkel van Nederland moet Maite Zubiaurre de laatste tijd veel aan één titel denken: Only the Paranoid Survive van Andy Grove. „Een aanrader. De centrale gedachte in dat boek is dat echt grote veranderingen in sectoren in één klap komen. Achteraf is dat duidelijk te herleiden: de ene ontwikkeling zette de andere in gang daarom is nu alles fundamenteel anders. Maar als je er middenin zit, zie je dat kantelpunt niet zo helder.” Zaak is die signalen wel helder te zien en de bedrijfsvoering zo om te gooien dat je sterker uit de storm komt, betoogt Grove. Hij schreef het boek in 1996 en was destijds topman van Intel. Dat bedrijf was eerst vooral succesvol met geheugenchips, tot er goedkopere concurrentie uit Japan kwam. Grove besloot tot een rigoureuze breuk en schakelde over op de productie van processoren. Intel zou vervolgens decennialang marktleider zijn. Het boek mag ouder zijn dan het bedrijf waar Zubiaurre (1983) leiding aan geeft – bol ging in 1999 van start – ze ziet parallellen met de situatie waarin haar webwinkelplatform zich bevindt. „Als je er op die manier naar kijkt, zie ik in de wereld van online winkelen nu de grootste verschuiving ooit.” Niet dat er al die jaren geen veranderingen waren. Bol breidde uit van een boekenwinkel naar een marktplaats waarop zo’n beetje alles te koop is. En de verkoper is niet meer alleen bol zelf, zo’n 60 procent van de verkopen gebeurt nu door externe handelaars. Klanten bezoeken de webshop niet meer via een computer in de hoek van de woonkamer, maar de hele dag door via een app op hun telefoon. „Industrieën blijven zich ontwikkelen. Dat zijn normale evoluties, optimalisaties”, zegt Zubiaurre. „Eigenlijk winkelt de online consument al 25 jaar op min of meer dezelfde manier. Consumenten kwamen binnen via een zoekbalk. We hebben mensen geleerd om resultaten te filteren en zo uit te komen bij het product dat ze zoeken. Significante disruptie hebben we niet echt gezien.” Nu is die disruptie er wel, zegt Zubiaurre. Ze haalt onderzoek van Deloitte aan waaruit blijkt dat meer dan de helft van de Nederlandse en Belgische consumenten AI gebruikt bij het online winkelen. „Dat is supersnel gegaan. En het zijn niet alleen jongeren, het zijn ook oma’s en boomers en millennials.” Klanten kunnen AI niet alleen om advies vragen over een product dat ze nodig hebben, ze kunnen het shoppen ook volledig uit handen geven. Gemeengoed is dat nog niet en de ervaringen met zelfstandig winkelende AI-agents zijn op zijn best wisselvallig te noemen. Maar het kan, en de technologie verbetert rap. Voor e-commercebedrijven betekent dat een grote verandering. Vrijwel allemaal hebben ze, net als bol, hun winkel georganiseerd rond een zoekbalk als toegangsdeur. Die leidt naar uitgebreide resultatenlijsten, waarin verkopers tegen betaling extra kunnen opvallen. Nu is dat een winstgevend model, maar voor het AI-tijdperk is iets nieuws nodig. Zubiaurre: „Bij de zoekbalk win je op gemak: een goed assortiment tegen een goede prijs en met een goede levertijd. Dat blijft belangrijk. Maar klanten zeggen: ’tot nu toe hielp je mij producten te vinden waarvan ik al wist dat ik ze nodig had’. Nu willen ze een winkelcompagnon, die je helpt identificeren wat je nodig hebt en dat vervolgens voor je koopt. „Ik denk dat de komende tien, twintig jaar vertrouwen belangrijker gaat worden. De consument vertrouwt AI niet. De bedrijven die gaan winnen, zijn niet per se die met de beste AI-modellen of de beste technologie.” In bol hebben klanten dat vertrouwen wel, denkt Zubiaurre. Eerder dit jaar introduceerde het bedrijf een op AI gebaseerde ‘shophulp’. „Wij zitten al 27 jaar in deze business. Dus wij weten best wel wat wel of niet een goed cadeau is voor een kind. Of een goede computer voor een puber op school, die er ook een beetje bij wil gamen. Wij weten veel. Met AI kunnen we die kennis nu inzetten om de klant echt te helpen, met de belofte dat het keer op keer goed komt.” De winkelreus probeert zijn merkbekendheid sinds kort ook op een andere manier in te zetten. Online verkopers kunnen op hun eigen webwinkel ook een afrekenknop met bol-logo zetten, waarbij bol de betaling verwerkt. „We hoorden van partners dat ze op hun eigen site problemen ervaren. Ze trekken daar klanten heen, maar die haken op het laatste moment af omdat ze die webshop niet kennen. Dan heeft een ondernemer al kosten gemaakt, maar geen omzet. Maar het merk bol wordt blind vertrouwd. Als dat er staat, zien handelaars hun omzet omhooggaan. Natuurlijk verdienen wij daar een fee aan, maar het is gekomen vanuit de behoefte om onze partners te helpen.” Ruim een jaar staat Zubiaurre nu aan het roer van bol. De positie ervan als lokale reus in Nederland en België is vrij uniek, ziet ze. In de meeste andere landen zijn internationale spelers als Amazon verreweg het grootst. „Als ik op reis ben en vertel wat bol is en wat onze marktpositie is, vragen mensen hoe dat mogelijk is. Wereldwijd zijn dit soort partijen er bijna niet.” Ook in Nederland probeert Amazon marktaandeel te veroveren. Daarvoor kondigde het Amerikaanse bedrijf vorig jaar een investering van 1,4 miljard euro aan. En dan is er de Chinese concurrentie, van goedkope winkels als Temu, maar sinds dit jaar ook in het hogere segment, bij Joybuy en TikTok Shop. „Er zijn alternatieven”, erkent Zubiaurre. „Voor mij is dat fighting spirit. Dan is het: wat kunnen wij doen? Een superieure ervaring brengen. Hop, ambitieniveau omhoog. Het houdt je superscherp. Daar hou ik van. In goede tijden leiden is makkelijker. Maar als het echt moet gebeuren, dan moet je je van je beste kant laten zien. „Wij zijn marktleider. Dat zeg ik niet zo graag, maar het is wel zo. We zijn een van de weinige partijen op Europees niveau die in een wereld met enorme concurrentie nog steeds wordt gekozen. Ik kan niet anders dan leunen op de superstevige positie die wij hebben. Maar het ergste wat wij kunnen doen, is denken: relax”, zegt Zubiaurre. „De ergste vijand van succes is zelfgenoegzaamheid”, parafraseert ze Grove. „Dat kan niet. In deze industrie kan dat niet. Zolang ik hier ben, gaat complacency niet gebeuren.” Die concurrentie is er niet alleen voor bol zelf, maar ook voor de circa 43.000 externe verkopers die op dit platform actief zijn. „Partners”, noemt Zubiaurre ze consequent. Zij concurreren met elkaar, met de verkooptak van bol en met buitenlandse concurrenten. Lange tijd liet bol alleen verkopers uit de Benelux toe, pas twee jaar terug mochten ook partijen uit de rest van de EU meedoen. En sinds vorig jaar mogen ook verkopers uit bijvoorbeeld China hun producten op bol zetten. Van alle partners komen er nu zo’n duizend van buiten de Benelux. Zubiaurre: „Wij waren zo’n beetje de laatste van de platformen die ze toelieten. We hebben heel lang vastgehouden aan alleen Belgische en Nederlandse partners; zij vormen nog steeds de overgrote meerderheid. Maar we zien ook: er is wereldwijde concurrentie, en als we over de grens kijken, zien we partijen die in bepaalde niches een goed aanbod hebben. We laten die met heel veel voorzichtigheid toe, we zijn zeer invested in Nederland en België. We willen absoluut goede kwaliteit blijven leveren.” De topvrouw weet dat het geen populaire boodschap is onder de lokale partners van het bedrijf. Bij een vakbeurs eerder dit jaar noemde ze het „de olifant in de kamer”. Ze vertelde op een podium over haar jeugd in Spanje en het familiebedrijf van haar vader. Hij maakte auto-onderdelen, en kreeg te maken met concurrentie uit Duitsland. „Hij kon niet meer op kosten concurreren. Dus is hij gepivot , hij ging onderdelen voor de vliegtuigindustrie maken.” Dat aanpassingsvermogen staat voor Zubiaurre centraal in ondernemerschap, vertelde ze een zaal vol webwinkeliers. Bols marktplaats heeft ook de aandacht van de Autoriteit Consument en Markt. Twee jaar lang deed de toezichthouder onderzoek naar het bedrijf. Wetsovertredingen zag de ACM niet, wel risico’s in de manier waarop bol de eigen retailtak kon voortrekken. Afgelopen augustus kwam er een ontwerpbesluit waarin bol bindende toezeggingen doet om die risico’s weg te nemen. Zo belooft het bedrijf data van zijn winkelplatform niet te gebruiken om de eigen verkooptak een voordeel te geven. „We begrijpen dat er vragen zijn over de manier waarop we als platform én verkoper opereren. Daar hebben we nu met de ACM afspraken over gemaakt”, zegt Zubiaurre. Dat er toezeggingen zijn gedaan, betekent volgens de topvrouw niet dat bol eerder zijn eigen aanbod voortrok. „Wij willen geen dingen doen die al bestaan. Als ons partnernetwerk een goed aanbod heeft, springen wij daar niet zelf als verkoper in. Maar als we het aanbod niet goed genoeg vinden, dan wel. Onze partners zijn er ook bij gebaat dat consumenten bol als de plek zien waar je altijd een goed aanbod vindt. Ons uitgangspunt is niet: bol moet groot worden, bol moet alles zelf doen.” Maak NRC jouw voorkeursbron op Google Bij Google kan je nu zelf aangeven welke nieuwsbronnen jij vaker wil zien in je zoekresultaten. But neither is his war on Iran, with oil prices climbing toward $120 a barrel and one U.S. lawmaker describing the administration’s plans for a renewed war on Iran as “insane.” Three weeks ago, in a telephone call with Russian President Vladimir Putin, Trump made a deal to purchase Russian diesel, which is forbidden under U.S. law. While the measure would have involved risible amounts of additional barrels into a strained global market, it has descended into farce. The three Russian tankers loaded with fuel may not be allowed to dock in U.S. ports. U.S. energy traders are unwilling to chance running afoul of long-standing sanctions against buying Russian energy. And Democratic lawmakers have said that any buyers will face congressional and legal scrutiny. The global benchmark price of oil, which was about $70 a barrel before Trump started the Iran war in February, rose to over $117 a barrel on Friday. U.S. nationwide average gasoline prices are $4.20 a gallon, more than a dollar higher than the year before; no president ever has kept gasoline above $4 more than Trump. Diesel, which powers the entire economy, is worse: At $6.32 a gallon, it is about 70 percent higher than one year ago. Another of Trump’s pro-Russia moves to keep energy prices in check was a pressure campaign on Kyiv to refrain from targeting Russian oil refineries with drones and missiles. U.S. negotiators including Steve Witkoff said that Kyiv should show “gratitude” toward Washington by curtailing strikes. Ukraine complied for a spell in October, before remembering that what Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky calls “long-range sanctions” are the country’s best way of severing the sinews of Russia’s war machine. Overnight Thursday, Ukraine resumed strikes on Russian oil targets, with a devastating attack on a large Rosneft refinery that makes jet fuel for the military. U.S. leverage over Ukraine is less than it used to be, since the Trump administration has not delivered any new military or financial assistance since Trump took office for a second time, and on several occasions, including this past month, has suspended what assistance there is, including some access to Starlink’s military-grade satellite internet service and intelligence sharing about inbound missile strikes. (While Ukraine has pleaded in vain for additional missile interceptors, the United States has pleaded poverty. This week, the United States sent a Patriot air defense system from Texas to Israel ahead of an anticipated restart to the fighting in the region.) The U.S. pivot to Russia isn’t limited to diesel deals and strong-arming Ukraine, though. In addition to stopping future aid, U.S. officials have reportedly been cautioning countries on the front line of Russia’s shadow war to tone down their warnings about Moscow’s hostile intentions. And on Friday, the U.S. welcomed Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov to the G-20 foreign ministers’ meeting in Atlanta, to the irritation of European allies. The abandonment of Ukraine has lately raised bristles in the European Parliament, where some politicians are redoubling their support for Ukraine even as Trump retreats. “This is not one of those instances of many different shades of gray. There’s clearly an aggressor who is in the wrong, and that’s Russia, and so I think, for me, that stands clearly,” said Reinier van Lanschot, a Dutch member of the European Parliament from the Volt Europa party and a vocal critic of Russia’s invasion. The war in Iran, which is now in its eighth month and likely to escalate in coming weeks, has kept oil prices high as shippers struggle to navigate a strait strewn with high costs, Iranian drones and missiles, and, for the first time, limpet mines .
